title: Party Night, Lan party inspired fun.
author: ThisIsKappa
selftext:
Hey r/aigamedev! Shameless self-promotion, but hopefully some free entertainment for you and your friends just like we had a lot of fun this Lan party using it.

**Party Night** ([https://partynight.host](https://partynight.host)) started as a game for our own LAN parties: a quick, chaotic thing to play together in the same room, with lots of shouting. It was so much fun that we kept building on it, and now it runs in the browser so anyone can join from anywhere.

Up to 6 players per room, and bots fill any empty seats. You roll a 1–100 die, zoom around a random board, and fight it out in short, frantic minigames between turns.

**What's in it right now**

* **34 minigames**, about a minute each: Full of randomness and chaos. Especially fun when we played them in the same room, some more entertaining than others. But improvements along the way made many of them quite fun. 
* Chaos modifiers: ice floors, fog, big heads, or everyone turned into chickens. Integrated with an OBS streaming overlay to have chatters force chaos modifiers on your lobby. 
* Knocked-out players come back as ghosts and throw tomatoes at the living Cartoon gore and a lot of flying hats 
* 240+ Cosmetics and pets 
* A live plaza where you can hang out, show off your outfit and jump into the next public match 
* Desktop and phone (touch controls), 
* Plus optional voice chat

No download and no account needed: you play as a guest and your progress is saved in your browser.

**How AI was used**

* **Code:** nearly all of it was written by AI coding agents (started in Codex, now mostly Claude Code), with us directing, playtesting and reviewing. Each minigame is a plugin (one server file, one browser file), so agents can build several at once on separate branches without stepping on each other. An [AGENTS.md](http://AGENTS.md) file keeps the conventions in one place.
*  **Art:** the illustrated style is a cutout rig built from SVG parts and recoloured at runtime, so 240+ cosmetics don't each need their own sprite sheet. 
* **Multiplayer:** the server runs all the gameplay and browsers only send input, which makes it much easier to keep an agent-written game in sync for everyone. 

**What we'd love feedback on**

1. Which minigames are fun, and which feel confusing or unfair? 
2. How does it play on your phone? 
3. Are the touch controls usable? 
4. Any lag or disconnects? (Roughly where in the world are you?) 
5. Did you know what to do in the first minute without help? 
6. Anything broken, ugly or annoying

It's still best with a group, just like at a LAN party. If you end up in a room full of bots, it might be less entertaining but who knows, hopefully you like it.

Thanks for trying!

comments.author: jojoba007
comments.body: Ah, really nice mini games online. UI needs a bit police, but for a first release so fun to play. You just have to click the link and start playing and join lobbies and play with friends!

replies.body: Thanks, will look to improve the UI and accessibility. Especially mobile is very rough to use.
